chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Ma'sum) from Safwan ibn Mihar from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abdullah ibn Muskhan from Ali ibn Abd al-'Aziz who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) performed the ritual bath for Ihram at Dhi al-Hulayfah, then said to his servants, 'Bring me what you have of game so that we may eat it.' Two birds were brought to him and he ate them.

The meaning in these narrations is that whoever performs the bath for Ihram and prays and says what he intends to say of the words after the prayer is not truly in reality in a state of Ihram, but rather he is one who has contracted the intention for Hajj and Umrah, and he enters into the state of being a Muhrim only when he says the Talbiyah.

And that which indicates this meaning is what Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar and others from whom Safwan narrated these narrations, meaning these preceding narrations, and said: 'They are widespread with us from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) that they said: When a man prays two rak'ahs and says what he intends to say of Hajj or Umrah in his place, then he has only made Hajj obligatory upon himself and contracted the contract of Hajj.'
And they said: 'Indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when he prayed in the Mosque of the Tree, he prayed and contracted the Hajj.'
And they did not say 'he prayed and contracted the Ihram', therefore it has become with us that there is no blame upon him for what he ate of that which is forbidden to the Muhrim.
And because it has come in the case of a man who eats game before he says the Talbiyah, having prayed and having said what he intends to say, but he has not said the Talbiyah.

And they said: Aban ibn Taghlib narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he eats the game and other than it, for he has only made obligatory upon himself what he said, so he is not allowed with us to return until he completes his Ihram.

For his obligation with us is a firm decision when he did what he did, he is not allowed to return to his family until he proceeds, and it is permissible for him before that and he may return whenever he wishes.

And when he makes Hajj obligatory upon himself then completes it with the Talbiyah, then the game and other than it have become forbidden to him and what is obligatory upon the Muhrim has become obligatory upon him in his action.

Because there are three things that can impose Ihram: announcing the intention, the Talbiyah, and the tying of the knot (of the garment). So when he does one of these three, he has entered into Ihram.
And if he performs the other manner before saying the Talbiyah, then he says the Talbiyah, he has made it obligatory.
The first place where a man makes the Talbiyah audible when he intends Hajj via the road of Al-Madain is Al-Bada', where the mile marker is; this was narrated.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَلْبِيَة: The ritual declaration of 'Here I am, O Allah'
key_terms.ذِي الْحُلَيْفَةِ: A specific Miqat (place of entering Ihram) near Mecca

ai.seo_question: When does the state of Ihram officially begin in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the Shia juristic distinction between the initial intention (*niyyah*) and the formal entry into the state of *Ihram*, asserting that prohibitions like hunting only bind after the *Talbiyah* is pronounced. It highlights the scholarly consensus that while the ritual bath and prayer establish the vow, the *Talbiyah* serves as the definitive act that transitions the pilgrim from a preparatory phase to a state of active sanctity, thereby making the consumption of game permissible prior to this declaration.
